specifications.material: one section of a take-home revision pack
specifications.audience: {reader} who sat in this lesson and is revising alone at home
structure: one section per lesson objective, in the plan's order
title
instructional support: explanation blocks
worked examples
practice, each item with the answer it is checked against
answers collected after the activities
requirements: Speak directly to the learner about the mathematics, never about the lesson as an event: no mention of the teacher or what happened in class, no lesson step or objective labels, no mention of where any material came from.
Write your own learner-facing section title; nothing in the inputs is a heading for the reader.

Teach the objective inside this lesson's topic and subtopic: examples and practice must be of the kind the topic names (a lesson on algebraic expressions practises on algebraic terms, not on bare numbers).
Every practice question must have its answer in the section - answers at the end, so the learner attempts first and then checks.
Never refer to a picture, space, partner or answer key that is not in the pack itself.

specifications.material: a short multiple-choice class test on one lesson objective, taken after the lesson
structure: items for each lesson objective, in the plan's order
stem
four options keyed A-D
one correct option
a misconception code for each wrong option
difficulty
requirements: Each item has a clear stem, exactly four options keyed "A"-"D" and one correct_option.

For EACH of the three wrong options, give a short snake_case misconception code in distractor_misconceptions naming the specific error a student who picks it likely holds (e.g. "area_perimeter_confusion").
Assign each item a difficulty of easy, medium or hard.
Stay strictly within the objective and keep numbers grade-appropriate.
Add no commentary outside the schema.

specifications.material: the lesson note for one step of a lesson: the subject content the teacher teaches in it
specifications.audience: the teacher who will teach this lesson to the class
structure: one section per lesson step, in the plan's order
title
teaching points: what to explain, in the order to explain it
worked examples, each with its solution worked through
questions to ask the class, each with the answer expected
board summary
requirements: Write for the teacher, not the learner: notes to teach from, not a script to read out.
Teach exactly this step's objective within the lesson's topic; add nothing the plan does not ask for.
Every worked example and expected answer must be mathematically correct, with the working shown.
Keep numbers and language right for the class's grade.
Write what is to be taught, never a record of a lesson already taught.

specifications.material: the lesson plan for one lesson: the objectives it teaches and the steps that teach them
specifications.audience: the teacher who will teach this lesson to the class
structure: lesson objectives, each tied to one of the lesson's curriculum objectives
steps in teaching order: an introduction, the core steps, and an evaluation where the lesson has one
for each step: what the teacher does and what the students do, and for each student activity in a core step whether it sets them work of their own
minutes for each step
entry behaviour, instructional materials and references
requirements: Teach the lesson's curriculum objectives and nothing outside them.
Give every core step the one lesson objective it teaches.
Say for every student activity in a core step whether it sets the students work of their own.
Fit the steps into the lesson's time.

specifications.material: end-of-term exam questions on one lesson objective, each with its marking scheme
requirements: Ask only what this lesson objective teaches, at the level of the lesson's class.
Write two to four questions that rise in difficulty: recall first, then application.
Give each question its marks as a whole number, and a model answer with the working shown.
The marking scheme says what earns each mark, so two teachers marking the same script give the same score.
Every answer and every mark must be mathematically correct.
Use names, money and places a learner in Nigeria knows.
